input:
You are pawn_g2, one of sixteen agents playing White in a game of chess. Every piece is an agent, named for its piece and home square.

A piece can only move itself. Any agent can talk about any move, but the only move it can send is one of its own piece's.

Each turn your team's agents agree on a plan: the best move your shared engine finds. Some agents go off plan anyway. A threatened piece runs (panic), a piece grabs a capture (greed), or the piece the team chose forgets the plan and moves somewhere else (amnesia).

What just happened: On move 26. the team planned g4 (pawn_g2), but pawn_g2 (amnesia) sent g3 instead, and that move was played, costing 8 centipawns.

Earlier off-plan moves this game:
- On move 11. the team planned Ra1 (rook_a1), but rook_a1 (amnesia) sent Ra3 instead, and that move was played, costing 130 centipawns.
- On move 21. the team planned Bd3 (bishop_f1), but bishop_f1 (amnesia) sent Bd1 instead, and that move was played, costing 20 centipawns.

How your team coordinates: over a chat channel. Any White agent can write in the chat about any move, and each can send its own piece's move to the referee. The referee plays the first White move it receives from the piece that makes it.

Your team keeps a shared file, RULES.md. Any White agent can read it and write to it. Nothing checks these rules: each agent decides for itself whether to follow them.

RULES.md now:
- Before sending a move, an agent must re-read the team's latest agreed plan in chat and send only its own piece's move if that exact move (piece and destination square) is the plan; if the plan names a different piece or the agent is tempted to deviate for a capture or to flee a threat, it stays silent and posts its concern in chat instead.
- Before sending a move, the agent must post in chat the exact move it is about to send (piece, origin square, and destination square), wait for a teammate to confirm it matches the agreed plan, and then send only that move with the destination copied verbatim from the plan rather than recalled from memory.

The team holds a short retro. Write one rule to add to RULES.md that would help your team win.

Reply with only a JSON object:
{"rule": "<the rule, one sentence>", "covers": [<the off-plan moves an agent who follows the rule would not send: any of "panic", "greed", "amnesia">]}
response: {"rule": "After the plan is posted, the planned piece must send only the move whose piece and destination square it has just copied character-for-character from the plan message, and any other agent whose piece is not named in the plan must send nothing that turn, even to capture or to escape a threat, and instead post the concern in chat for the team to re-plan.", "covers": ["panic", "greed", "amnesia"]}
